I have been doing this for 20 years on this same land. I know what works here in Quzhou. My son works in the city so it is mostly me managing the farm. I cannot waste money or take risks.

My 8 mu rotates wheat and maize on the same fields — winter wheat in, summer maize after. I use the whole 8 mu for both, one after the other. That is how we have always done it here.

For wheat, I will use the improved variety seeds — the local agricultural station has been pushing Kenong-type seeds for years and my neighbors who use them do better than those still keeping old seed. I apply urea and compound fertilizer the way my husband and I figured out over the years — a base application before planting, then topdress at jointing. I irrigate at seeding if the soil is dry, again at jointing, and at heading. Three times is usually enough with my well. I spray twice — once for weeds in winter, once for aphids and mildew before heading. I do rotary tillage before wheat goes in.

For maize, I use hybrid seed — everyone does, the yields are much better, I learned this early. After I harvest the wheat in June I am tired and the weather is hot, so I do no-tillage and seed the maize directly. This saves my back and saves time. I apply fertilizer at planting and topdress once at the big bell stage. I only irrigate maize if it looks stressed — usually twice is enough. I spray herbicide early and watch for corn borer later.

With just the two of us and my son gone, I keep things simple and mechanized where I can.
